neet_che_u10_t02_1.working: Chlorine has the most negative electron gain enthalpy (about -349 kJ/mol). Fluorine is less negative because its small, compact 2p shell causes electron–electron repulsion.

neet_che_u10_t02_2.working: Approximate IE1 values (kJ/mol): B 801, Al 577, Ga 579, In 558, Tl 589. This gives B > Tl > Ga > Al > In, because poor d/f shielding raises IE1 for Ga and Tl.

neet_che_u10_t02_3.working: Boiling points (°C): PH3 -88, AsH3 -62, NH3 -33, SbH3 -17, BiH3 about +17. NH3 is raised by hydrogen bonding but still boils below SbH3 and BiH3.

neet_che_u10_t02_4.working: Because of the inert pair effect, Tl+ is more stable than Tl3+ (Tl3+ is oxidising). So A is false and R is true.

neet_che_u10_t02_5.working: IE1 of Pb (about 715 kJ/mol) is higher than Sn (about 708 kJ/mol), due to lanthanide contraction and poor f shielding, so I is true. S has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than O because O is small and suffers electron repulsion, so II is true.
